text:
maria: Quick follow-up to the pagination/retries RFC — pairing with @olivia yesterday uncovered a couple of cross-lang tradeoffs we should decide on now.

ankit: TL;DR? what are the open knobs?

maria: Mostly: 1) where to draw the line between transport-level retries vs client-level retries, 2) default retry/backoff config across Python/TS/Go, 3) iterator ergonomics for pagination (resume tokens vs page tokens + prefetch semantics), 4) streaming resume/idempotency guarantees.

olivia: I sketched proposals: unify a small RetryPolicy object across SDKs (max_retries, initial_backoff, max_backoff, jitter, retry_on_codes). Transport implementations adapt it.

jordan: Sounds good. For Go we prefer explicit RetryOpts struct. For TS/Python prefer a single class/function with defaults. We should avoid hidden global state.

maria: Agreed. My other callout: transports should only retry low-level network/connectivity errors and 5xx by default. 429s and rate-limits should be surfaced to the client policy so the app can opt to back off more aggressively or route to fallback model.

ankit: So transport-level: connect/reset/timeouts + idempotent GET-like ops. Client-level: 429, application-level idempotency (retries that might reapply a mutation). Makes sense.

olivia: Proposed default RetryPolicy (conservative):
```python
RetryPolicy(
  max_retries=4,
  initial_backoff_ms=150,
  max_backoff_ms=2500,
  jitter=true,
  retry_on=["timeout","5xx","connection_error"]
)
```
This is the baseline cross-lang default; allow per-call overrides.

jordan: For TypeScript example I'd expose it as an options bag: `{ retry: { maxRetries: 4, baseMs: 150, maxMs: 2500, jitter: true } }` and provide `client.withRetry(policy)` helper.

maria: Pagination: two patterns we must support: page-token (stateless) and cursor/resume-token (stateful, opaque). Recommendation: server returns `next_page_token` OR `resume_token`. Client iterators should prefer resume_token when present because it allows resuming long-running scans, but we must document idempotency constraints.

ankit: Implementation notes: iterators should offer `prefetchPages` / `maxInFlight` knobs. Default prefetch=1 for low memory. Provide async iterator + helper `collectPages(maxPages)` across languages.

olivia: Also proposal for streamed responses: if a stream is interrupted, server MAY return an opaque resume token in trailing metadata. Client should surface `stream_resume_token` to user and have `resume_stream(token)` API. Mark resume as best-effort: server may re-send overlapping items; require consumers to be prepared for duplicates unless server guarantees otherwise.

maria: On idempotency for retries: for non-idempotent requests we require callers to pass an idempotency key (GUID) if they want safe retry across retries/failover. We should add helper util to generate stable idempotency keys in SDKs.

jordan: Small Go API sketch: `type RetryPolicy struct { MaxRetries int; BaseBackoff time.Duration; MaxBackoff time.Duration; Jitter bool; RetryOn []string }` and `client.Call(ctx, req, WithRetry(policy))`.

olivia: Small TS sketch:
```ts
const client = new RedwoodClient({ retry: defaultRetry });
for await (const page of client.listFoo({ pageSize: 100 })) { /* ... */ }
// to resume
client.listFoo({ resumeToken: token });
```

maria: Decision log (arch-rfc-bot): unify RetryPolicy shape; transport only retries low-level/connectivity + 5xx by default; client-level handles 429 and application semantics; expose resume tokens and resume_stream API; provide prefetch/max_inflight knobs with conservative defaults. :white_check_mark:

arch-rfc-bot: Decision recorded: "SDK surface: unified RetryPolicy + explicit resume token semantics + conservative prefetch defaults".

ankit: One more: migration path. If we tighten defaults, apps that relied on aggressive transport retry may see more surface 429s. We'll add a compatibility flag `legacy_transport_retries=true` for one minor release.

maria: Good call — I'll draft the RFC update and include language for migration, sample code in Python/TS/Go, and a small test matrix for idempotency/resume scenarios. Ping @jordan and @ankit for API review on Go/TS shapes.

jordan: I'll review this afternoon.

olivia: I'll draft the sample code snippets for the docs.

maria: Thanks team — I'll open the PR with the decision + API sketches. :rocket:
